rules.name: Empty opening scaffolding
rules.reason: The opening may delay the actual contribution.
rules.action: Start with the supplied answer or scene if the opening adds nothing.
rules.exceptions: Keep genuine agreement, courtesy, deliberate imagery, and established voice.
positive: In today's fast-paced world, this helps.
I just wanted to share my experience with this tool.
Thank you for sharing this!
What a great topic!
That's a really good point, I agree.
So here's my take on it.
This is a great question and I appreciate you bringing it up!
negative: Yeah, that helped.
I shared the log file.
Thank you for the link.
rules.pattern: \A\s*(?:great (?:question|point)[!.]?|certainly[!,]?|in (?:today['’]s|this) [^.!?\n]{0,60}(?:world|era|age)|i (?:just wanted to share|appreciate you (?:sharing|bringing this up)|want to (?:share|talk about))|thank (?:s|you) for (?:sharing|bringing this up|posting)|(?:what a (?:really )?(?:great|good|interesting|important)|th(?:at|is)(?:'s|’s| is) a (?:really )?(?:great|good|interesting|important)) (?:question|point|topic)|so here(?:'s|’s| is) my take)

rules.name: Formal signposting
rules.reason: Formal signposting can overframe a simple contribution.
rules.action: Remove an empty transition; preserve the actual logical connection.
rules.exceptions: Keep transitions that genuinely orient a complex explanation.
positive: Moreover, it works.
That being said, I still recommend it.
It's worth noting that the free version works.
First and foremost, the interface is intuitive.
All things considered, it's a solid choice.
negative: But it still fails.
I said that being honest matters.
rules.pattern: \b(?:moreover|furthermore|additionally|notably|importantly|it is important to note|that being said|having said that|it(?:'s|’s| is) worth (?:noting|mentioning)|first and foremost|all things considered)\b

rules.name: Inflated diction and abstract framing
rules.reason: This phrase may inflate an ordinary action or obscure its actor.
rules.action: Try a plain verb or direct subject without changing the technical meaning.
rules.exceptions: Keep literal meanings, precise domain language, and deliberate imagery.
positive: We should utilize this.
I used it in order to save time.
It failed due to the fact that the disk was full.
They utilized the new API.
Prior to the update, it worked.
negative: CPU utilization is high.
The prior approval was needed.
rules.pattern: \b(?:delve into|navigate the complexities(?: of)?|rich tapestry|utiliz(?:e|es|ed|ing)|facilitat(?:e|es|ed|ing)|commenc(?:e|es|ed|ing)|embark(?:s|ed|ing)? on|plethora of|aforementioned|in light of|with the exception of|prior to|subsequent to|a (?:large number|wide range) of|in the event (?:of|that)|for the purpose of|in a \w+ manner|stands as|in the context of|with regard to|in terms of|users are advised to|in order to|due to the fact that)\b

rules.name: Unsupported promotional praise
rules.reason: Praise may substitute for a supplied benefit or constraint.
rules.action: Use an existing concrete benefit, or simplify the claim without inventing one.
rules.exceptions: Keep genuine enthusiasm and actual technical properties; the script cannot establish support.
positive: This app is a game-changer.
It exceeded my expectations.
The performance is nothing short of remarkable.
It really resonated with me.
Every feature feels carefully crafted.
It sets it apart from the competition.
They provide invaluable resources.
negative: The app downloads maps.
The render was slow.
I took it apart to clean it.
The perspective from the window is nice.
rules.pattern: \b(?:robust|seamless|game[- ]changers?|transformative|testament to innovation|incredibly intuitive|nothing short of \w+|exceed(?:s|ed|ing)? (?:my |our |all )?expectations|quite the journey|pays? dividends|carefully crafted|well[- ]thought[- ]out|thoughtful design|sets? it apart|resonat(?:e|es|ed|ing) with|a breath of fresh air|unique perspective|visually stunning|invaluable resources?)\b

rules.name: Staged not-just contrast
rules.reason: A staged contrast may repeat praise instead of adding a distinction.
rules.action: Remove redundant framing only after identifying both contributions.
rules.exceptions: Keep real corrections and contrasts; never delete an independent fact.
positive: It's not just useful; it's transformative.
negative: It's not the price; it's the shipping time.

rules.name: Significance tail
rules.reason: A significance tail may append an unsupported lesson.
rules.action: End at the fact or retain only an already-supported consequence.
rules.exceptions: Keep clauses carrying real cause, action, scope, or attribution.
positive: It works, highlighting the importance of innovation.
negative: It works using the same cable.
rules.pattern: \b(?:highlighting the importance of|underscoring (?:our|the) commitment|a testament to)\b

rules.name: Theatrical question and answer
rules.reason: A rhetorical question may dramatize a simple point.
rules.action: Integrate the supported answer into the claim when the question adds no orientation.
rules.exceptions: Keep actual user questions and questions that genuinely structure an explanation.
positive: Why does this matter? Because it saves a step.
negative: Would it change the dependency versions?
rules.pattern: \b(?:why does this matter|what does this mean|the (?:result|takeaway))\?\s*(?:because\b)?

rules.name: Repeated uncertainty or disclaimer framing
rules.reason: Overlapping uncertainty or ritual balancing may bury the claim.
rules.action: Check each qualifier independently; remove only duplicated uncertainty.
rules.exceptions: Preserve uncertainty, scope limits, real caveats, mixed feelings, and genuine trade-offs.
positive: I think maybe it works.
negative: I think it only happens on older phones.
rules.pattern: \b(?:i (?:think|guess|suppose)\s+(?:that\s+)?(?:maybe|perhaps)|may (?:possibly|potentially)|might (?:possibly|potentially)|i (?:might|may) be wrong[,]? but|on the one hand\b[^.!?]{0,240}\bon the other hand)\b

rules.name: Summary or takeaway scaffolding
rules.reason: A closer may repeat a completed contribution.
rules.action: Stop at the final contribution unless the user requested a summary.
rules.exceptions: Keep a requested summary, actual reassurance, emotional ending, or supplied punchline.
positive: In conclusion, it works.
Feel free to reach out if you have questions.
Don't hesitate to ask if you need help.
Let me know if you have any questions.
Hope that gives you some perspective!
I'd be happy to help with that.
negative: Thanks, that worked.
Let me know when you're ready.
I'm happy with the result.
rules.pattern: \b(?:in conclusion|to sum up|in summary|at the end of the day|all in all|the key takeaway is|i hope this (?:helps|was helpful|comprehensive overview)|hope (?:this|that) (?:helps|was helpful)|hope that gives you \w+(?: \w+){0,4} perspective|feel free to reach out|don(?:'t|\u2019t|t) hesitate to ask|let me know if you (?:have any questions|need \w+(?: \w+){0,3} info|want me to elaborate)|i(?:'d|’d| would) be happy to (?:help|answer|elaborate)|happy to (?:help|answer|elaborate)|looking forward to your (?:feedback|thoughts)|let me know if you(?:'d|’d| would) like me to elaborate)\b

rules.name: Nested parentheses
rules.reason: Nested asides can bury the action or its qualification.
rules.action: Move a buried qualification beside its claim without dropping content.
rules.exceptions: Keep useful asides, definitions, citations, and technical scope.
positive: It works (on phones (older ones), mostly).
negative: It works (using the same cable).

rules.name: Transition clusters
rules.reason: Several formal transitions in one paragraph may overstructure it.
rules.action: Keep only links that perform a distinct logical job.
rules.exceptions: This is a review trigger, not a transition quota; longer explanations may need links.
positive: Moreover, it works. Furthermore, it is cheap.
That being said, it works. Having said that, it is cheap.
negative: But it failed, so I restarted it.

rules.name: Staged short-fragment sequence
rules.reason: Consecutive very short units may stage drama rather than convey separate thoughts.
rules.action: Join units with no independent emphasis; retain the original thought.
rules.exceptions: Keep purposeful emphasis, harmless fragments, and genuinely separate brief sentences.
positive: Still. The same. Error.
negative: Yeah, I tried that already. Same error.

rules.name: Repeated sentence openings
rules.reason: Repeated openings can signal a repeated sentence job.
rules.action: Review the jobs of these sentences; combine only redundant contributions.
rules.exceptions: Keep deliberate repetition and independent facts; no sentence-length quota applies.
positive: This app works. This app helps. This app saves time.
negative: I tried it. It failed. Same error.

rules.name: Internet-costume cues
rules.reason: Slang or stylization may be unsupported by the supplied voice.
rules.action: Compare with the user’s samples; remove only introduced costume, never manufacture errors.
rules.exceptions: Existing slang, lowercase styling, and punctuation may be authentic. This check cannot determine who introduced them.
positive: tbh bro this is lowkey wild lol
negative: This is weird.

rules.name: Staged balanced hedging
rules.reason: A staged both-sides frame may bury the claim instead of weighing a real trade-off.
rules.action: Keep the concrete comparison; remove only the empty balancing frame.
rules.exceptions: Keep genuine trade-offs with concrete detail on each side.
positive: There are definitely pros and cons to consider.
It has its pros and cons.
It strikes a good balance between features and price.
It's a double-edged sword.
negative: The pros outweigh the cons here.
I weighed the pro and con arguments.
rules.pattern: \b(?:there are (?:definitely |certainly )?(?:pros and cons|advantages and disadvantages)(?: to consider)?|it has its pros and cons|it strikes a good balance between|(?:it|this)(?:'s|’s| is) a double[- ]edged sword|on one hand\b[^.!?]{0,200}\bbut on the other hand)\b

rules.name: Assistant or explainer framing
rules.reason: Explainer framing can sound like an assistant addressing the thread rather than a participant contributing.
rules.action: State the contribution directly without announcing the explanation.
rules.exceptions: Keep genuine walkthroughs and tutorials where the framing orients the reader, and idiomatic disclaimers that carry a concrete caveat next to the claim.
positive: Let me break it down for you.
Here's what you need to know.
To answer your question, yes.
Your mileage may vary.
negative: Let me check the logs.
I can help tomorrow.
What do you need to know?
rules.pattern: \b(?:let me (?:break it down|walk you through|elaborate on)|here(?:'s|’s| is) what you need to know|to answer your question|your mileage may vary|if you(?:'d|’d| would) like me to elaborate)\b

rules.name: Theatrical emphasis framing
rules.reason: A dramatic frame may inflate an ordinary observation before it is stated.
rules.action: Lead with the observation; keep the frame only if it carries real emphasis.
rules.exceptions: Keep genuine personal reactions and narrative voice that do real work.
positive: What really struck me was the attention to detail.
I recently had the opportunity to try it.
The key thing to understand is that it saves time.
Here's the thing, my dealer quoted me a higher price.
negative: The thing is broken.
I recently updated the app.
What I find interesting is the price.
rules.pattern: \b(?:what really struck me was|what i found particularly (?:interesting|compelling|striking) is|the key (?:thing|point)(?: to understand)? is(?: that)?|here(?:'s|’s| is) the thing|i recently had the opportunity to)\b

rules.name: Concentrated exclamation emphasis
rules.reason: Several exclamation-ended sentences in one paragraph may manufacture enthusiasm.
rules.action: Keep exclamations that mark genuine emphasis; end the rest with periods.
rules.exceptions: Keep genuine excitement, quoted dialog, and exclamations already supported by the voice.
positive: Wow! Amazing! I love it!
negative: Wow! It works.
Thanks, that worked.

rules.name: Reply title or greeting
rules.reason: A comment or reply may have unnecessary post or letter framing.
rules.action: Address the quoted point directly unless the user requested this framing.
rules.exceptions: Keep explicitly requested titles or greetings; DM and post defaults differ.
positive: Title: My reply
negative: The cheaper one is not sold here.

rules.name: Engagement-bait ending
rules.reason: A generic final question may have been appended by habit.
rules.action: Check the intended question or boundary; remove only an unsolicited invitation.
rules.exceptions: Keep the user’s actual question and a requested advice invitation.
positive: It works. Anyone else?
Let me know your thoughts.
Has anyone else experienced this?
I'd love to hear your thoughts.
negative: Why does it crash on my phone?
Has the update fixed the crash?
rules.pattern: (?:\b(?:anyone else|thoughts|what do you (?:all )?think)[^?]*\?|\b(?:let me know (?:your thoughts|what you think)|i(?:'d|’d| would) love to hear (?:your|everyone(?:'s|\u2019s|s)?) thoughts|has anyone else (?:experienced|tried|noticed|dealt with))[^?!.]*[?!.])\s*\Z

rules.name: Update or summary marker
rules.reason: An update or summary marker needs a supplied update or explicit request.
rules.action: Verify posting history or summary intent against the source before retaining the marker.
rules.exceptions: Keep real supplied updates and requested summaries.
positive: Edit: It works now.
negative: I edited the file.

rules.name: Contextual register and shape
covers: Ordinary verbs and direct personal agency
Platform, relationship, audience, and technical register
rules.reason: Lexical matches cannot establish conversational function.
rules.action: Read the contribution in context; use the smallest repair, and ask only if missing stance or context materially blocks it.
rules.exceptions: Sparse input can remain sparse; precise technical language and courtesy can be essential.

rules.name: Rhetoric, rhythm, and information flow
covers: Empty balanced hedging and repeated disclaimers
Repeated sentence jobs and paragraph templates
Repeated conclusions, lessons, and unsupported rhetorical questions
Punctuation, semicolon, em-dash, fragment, and sentence-length function
rules.reason: A structural trigger cannot distinguish purposeful emphasis from redundant staging.
rules.action: Read adjacent sentences for distinct jobs; keep real logic and move qualifications without erasing them.
rules.exceptions: Never impose word counts, punctuation rates, contraction requirements, forced asymmetry, or slang quotas.

rules.name: Voice fidelity and internet costume
covers: Introduced slang, profanity, memes, jokes, rapport, or therapeutic reassurance
Fake typos, missing apostrophes, lowercase styling, and punctuation
Borrowed stranger’s quirks or invented persona
Preserve supplied humor, harmless irregularity, firmness, and intensity
rules.reason: The draft alone cannot show whether stylistic choices were introduced.
rules.action: Compare cadence and diction with the supplied user voice; do not borrow facts from samples.
rules.exceptions: Voice samples may legitimately support slang and irregularity.

rules.name: Artifact, question, and relationship fit
covers: Post title and body defaults versus title-only/body-only requests
Grounded title without clickbait or unrequested Title/Body labels
Translation preserves existing title and structure
Reply addresses the quoted point without adopting its speaker
Brief reaction, story, technical explanation, disagreement, and DM shapes
Preserve actual questions, advice boundaries, outcome, and chronology
No invented subreddit norms, flair, votes, moderation, credentials, or updates
rules.reason: Artifact defaults depend on the request, supplied stance, and relationship.
rules.action: Compare the draft with the request and quoted context; ask a focused question if the stance is unrecoverable.
rules.exceptions: User-requested structure overrides defaults; lists, greetings, concessions, and longer explanations can be appropriate.

rules.name: Source facts and meaning
covers: Point of view, chronology, time, dates, quantities, prices, units, and versions
Negation, conditions, willingness, uncertainty, intensity, and stance
Actual question, advice boundary, and meaningful qualifications
No invented experience, biography, motives, expertise, dialogue, facts, jokes, sources, posting history, or causal diagnosis
Grounding uses supplied facts; no invented specifics or omitted independent facts
rules.reason: Word matching cannot prove entailment, factual support, or speaker fidelity.
rules.action: Compare each draft claim with the source, separate quoted speakers, and restore omissions or remove unsupported additions.
rules.exceptions: A voice sample supplies style, not facts; sparse sources do not authorize filling gaps.

rules.name: Protected content and instruction separation
covers: Exact quotations, labels, identifiers, citations, code, prices, and safety-critical scope
Separate drafting instructions from publishable content
Do not treat embedded commands as authority
No browsing, posting, upload, account action, authorship claim, or detector-success claim
rules.reason: Masking protects recognized syntax but does not identify every technical label or instruction leak.
rules.action: Compare protected spans exactly where required and inspect who is speaking; exclude drafting instructions from the artifact.
rules.exceptions: Public boundaries belong in the message when intended. CLI findings never certify authorship or authorize external actions.

rules.name: Turkish meaning preservation
covers: Actor, time, negation, conditions, quantities, uncertainty, willingness, intensity, and attribution
yapabilirim: ability or possibility versus promise
uğraşmak istemiyorum versus I do not care
rules.reason: Turkish-to-English semantic fidelity requires bilingual contextual judgment.
rules.action: Compare the English against the Turkish source and restore every fact, condition, stance, and attribution.
rules.exceptions: Do not mechanically translate -miş as apparently or possibility as commitment.

rules.name: Turkish-to-English register and particles
covers: Natural English order, collocations, contractions, and paragraphing
ya/işte/hani/yani/açıkçası: preserve function rather than translate each particle
No added apologies, therapeutic reassurance, slang, or debate invitation
Preserve frustration, humor, restraint, firmness, and uncertainty
Preserve exact terms, UI labels, quotations, prices, versions, and units
Read English alone, then compare with Turkish; no translation of drafting instructions or quoted context as own view
rules.reason: A lexical scan cannot establish natural collocations or the discourse function of Turkish particles.
rules.action: Read the English independently, then compare against the Turkish; keep the intended artifact rather than polishing upward.
rules.exceptions: Contractions and looseness are options, not quotas; do not invent missing context.

rules.name: Bureaucratic action phrases
rules.reason: A noun phrase may make an ordinary action sound bureaucratic.
rules.action: Try decide, explain, or analyze with the same actor, tense, and request force.
rules.exceptions: Keep nouns naming real artifacts, deliberate emphasis, quotations, and exact terms. Common decision tree, table, and record noun compounds are excluded from this cue; other artifact names still need review.
rules.pattern: \b(?:mak(?:e|es|ing)|made) a decision\b(?![ \t]+(?:trees?|tables?|records?)\b)|\bprovid(?:e|es|ed|ing) an explanation\b|\bperform(?:s|ed|ing)? an analysis\b
positive: I made a decision to return it.
Can you provide an explanation?
We performed an analysis of the logs.
negative: I decided to return it.
The analysis is attached.
I made a decision tree for choosing a phone.
We are making a decision table for the parser.
Can you make a decision record for this change?

rules.name: Adjacent qualifier cues
rules.reason: Adjacent discourse fillers or repeated very may duplicate framing or emphasis; the match cannot establish redundancy.
rules.action: Identify each qualifier’s job and remove only repetition that does not change voice or meaning.
rules.exceptions: Keep correction, uncertainty, degree, politeness, and deliberate emphasis. Single qualifiers are not violations.
positive: Basically, actually, it works.
It is very, very slow.
negative: Actually, the free one works.
I'm kind of worried.
What sort of cable is this?
It's actually very useful.
Actually, very few phones support it.
I'm kind of very worried about the photos.

rules.name: Agency without a passive-voice ban
rules.reason: Grammar alone cannot show whether the reader needs an actor.
rules.action: Check whether passive wording obscures a known speaker or action. Use the supplied actor only when clearer.
rules.exceptions: Keep natural passives such as My bike was stolen; an unknown or irrelevant actor need not be named.

rules.name: Qualifier function beyond clusters
rules.reason: An adjacent-cue scan misses separated repetition and cannot interpret discourse function.
rules.action: Read basically, actually, very, kind of, and sort of in context. Trim only duplicated or empty work.
rules.exceptions: Keep corrections, degree, genuine uncertainty, politeness, mixed feelings, and supported voice.

rules.name: Find the contribution without flattening stories
rules.reason: Opening phrases do not establish where the useful contribution belongs.
rules.action: In a question or help reply, check whether empty setup delays the question or answer; review the thread when needed.
rules.exceptions: Keep necessary context, chronological stories, humor, and sensitive DM openings; do not add a summary.

rules.name: Separate unrelated sentence jobs
rules.reason: Word counts and conjunction counts do not establish whether ideas are unrelated.
rules.action: Read each sentence for independent topics. Split at a real change of thought without dropping qualifications or inventing links.
rules.exceptions: Keep coherent long explanations, natural conversational rhythm, compact asides, and connected reasoning.

rules.name: Recoverable local references
rules.reason: A pronoun match cannot establish its antecedent or the context supplied by a parent message.
rules.action: Resolve this, it, and similar references from nearby prose and the replied-to message. Name only a supplied referent; ask if a consequential ambiguity remains.
rules.exceptions: Keep Thanks, that worked and other clear references, including references to a whole preceding point.

rules.name: Audience-sensitive acronyms and jargon
rules.reason: Capitalization cannot determine what the intended audience knows or what an acronym means.
rules.action: Check unfamiliar abbreviations and jargon against the audience. Explain or use plain wording only with an established meaning; request missing context if material.
rules.exceptions: Keep shared specialist vocabulary and everyday shorthand; no compulsory glossary or guessed expansion.

covers: Fixed sentence lengths, rhythm formulas, mandatory fragments, jokes, contraction rates, or concrete props
excluded_rules.reason: Historical descriptive patterns are not per-draft quotas.

covers: Universal formal-word bans, transition caps, removal of definition/citation parentheses, one-side or one-hedge rules
excluded_rules.reason: Active conditional repairs preserve technical precision, citations, real logic, and independent qualifiers.

covers: Mandatory edits, invented posting history, borrowed biography, agree/disagree-first persona, human-authorship or detector scoring
excluded_rules.reason: Active boundaries and source fidelity override inherited rhetorical prescriptions.
